clue.text: Fellow was first to get kept out, being jeered at

indicators.note: kept means held inside, so the word for being first holds the little word out

parts.note: someone who was first led the field
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fellow who once led the pack is now shut out of the group and mocked for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept' looks like part of 'kept out', meaning excluded; it is the container signal, and 'out' is just the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Flouting someone is mocking them openly, so being scorned or jeered at is having been flouted.

clue.text: One is able to follow saint of the church

indicators.note: follow tells us the pieces for one and is able come after the saint's name

parts.note: St Basil the Great, a Church Father
I is the Roman numeral for one
can means is able

explanation.surface: Someone capable of following a saint's example within the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a kind of large church, and the adjective describes something belonging to such a building.

clue.text: Moderate Anglicans in a bit of a depression

indicators.note: in places the Anglicans' letters inside the small hollow

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow in a surface
CE stands for the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: Middle-of-the-road churchgoers feeling a little low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' reads as low mood; here it is a physical hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent can mean fair or reasonable in amount, a moderate rather than excessive level.

clue.text: Substance in biology or botany I'd mistaken

indicators.note: mistaken suggests the letters of botany I'd are wrongly arranged and need sorting

explanation.surface: A student confuses a biology term with a botany one.
explanation.definitionFit: An antibody is a protein made by the immune system, a key substance studied in biology.

clue.text: Ma came and sauntered around seaside attraction maybe

indicators.note: around tells us the letters of Ma came and sauntered are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Mum arrived and strolled about at the seaside, where some attraction lay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two parts of the fodder and is not part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Coin-operated game halls are a typical feature of British seafront resorts, an example of a seaside attraction.

clue.text: Understood tea-brewer could be uncommunicative

parts.note: tacit means understood without being stated
an urn is a large vessel for making tea

explanation.surface: Someone who quietly makes the tea in an office may seem reserved.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person says little, being reserved and reluctant to talk.

clue.text: Learner to flap around and grumble

indicators.note: around puts the word for flapping on both sides of the learner's letter

parts.note: to beat wings is to flap them
L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: A trainee gets into a panic and complains.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleat is to complain in a feeble, whining way, a synonym for moaning.

clue.text: Artist's close-fitting undergarment

definitions.meaning: a drawer is one who draws, so an artist's (artist is) can be read as ...
knickers or underpants, an old word for underwear

explanation.definitionFit: One who draws is a sketcher or illustrator, and the plural word also names knickers worn under clothes.

clue.text: Place free from trouble brings delight

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for Place in street names
to ease is to relieve from pain or worry

explanation.surface: A trouble-free spot brings joy.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to gratify them, a synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Mules can wander around America

indicators.note: wander suggests the letters of mules can roam into a new order

explanation.surface: Pack animals roam about across the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is a link here, rounding out the picture of wandering animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure in a star-spangled hat is the personification of the US government and nation.

clue.text: Company vehicles outside home on Sabbath

indicators.note: outside puts the vehicles around the word for at home

parts.note: buses are public road vehicles
in means at home

explanation.surface: A firm's vans are parked outside the house on Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm or enterprise is a business, a synonym for a commercial company.

clue.text: State the reason for wearing this tie

indicators.note: wearing means the words state the reason have the answer on them, carried within

explanation.surface: Asked to explain why you have on this particular necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a rope or chain that ties an animal to a post.

clue.text: One after another tries with aim amiss

indicators.note: amiss shows the letters of tries and aim have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes repeated shots and keeps missing the target.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin adverb means in a series, point by point, taking things in order.

clue.text: Member of aristocracy that is good man ahead of all others

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
ie, from Latin id est, means that is
ST, saint, is the crossword convention for a good man

explanation.surface: A nobleman, a virtuous one, takes precedence over everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliest means first in time, before any rival.

clue.text: In class busy little worker may be a sneak

parts.note: taken as written
a form is a school class in Britain
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A diligent pupil in a school class could be the one telling tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak is a telltale, someone who passes on information about others.

clue.text: "Leader needs policy" — what you see in newspaper?

parts.note: a head is a leader or chief
a line is a party policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A banner quote about a leader demanding a policy appears in print.
explanation.definitionFit: The large-type title over a news story is the first thing a reader sees on the page.

clue.text: Noisy fellow following scheme

indicators.note: following places the man's word after the scheme

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
gent is short for gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A loud man trails after a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, resonant, often mournful sound.

clue.text: Be like a Pobble, they say, when it comes to sugar

indicators.note: they say signals the sound of the phrase is what is wanted, not its spelling

parts.note: Edward Lear's nonsense poem The Pobble Who Has No Toes, so to be like him is to lack toes

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about Lear's toeless creature and sweet things.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pobble is from an Edward Lear nonsense poem about a creature that loses its toes.
explanation.definitionFit: The milk sugar is a disaccharide found in dairy products.

clue.text: Sort of design clients ordered

indicators.note: ordered tells us the letters of clients are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Customers commissioned a particular pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-out template is used to paint lettering or patterns, so it gives a kind of design.

clue.text: Miscellanea everyone classifies

parts.note: all means everyone
sorts means arranges into categories

explanation.surface: Everybody files away odds and ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture of various kinds, as in liquorice sweets of that name, is an assortment of miscellaneous items.

clue.text: Machine without love or hate

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside puts the machine around the zero

parts.note: a lathe is a machine tool for turning
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A mechanic with no affection for a machine feels only hatred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside, the machine wrapping O.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to detest intensely, a stronger synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Bill, very dry little creature

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
arid means very dry

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill is extremely dry.
explanation.definitionFit: An acarid is a mite or tick, a tiny arachnid.

clue.text: Female educated to hold a lasso

indicators.note: to hold means the woman's name wraps around the single letter

parts.note: Educating Rita is Willy Russell's play and film about a woman's education

explanation.surface: A schooled woman is given a rope to grasp.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a British play and film about a hairdresser who studies literature.
explanation.definitionFit: A riata is a long rope with a noose used by cowboys, the same thing as a lariat.

clue.text: Male icon working in pit

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of male icon are put to work in another order

explanation.surface: A famous man is employed underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit is the British term for a colliery, where coal is dug.

clue.text: Boy joins a girl to make music

parts.note: a son is a boy
Tina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A lad teams up with a lass to perform a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonatina is a short, simple sonata, a piece of instrumental music.

clue.text: Female bird nibbled plant

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
bit means nibbled

explanation.surface: A hen pecked at some greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Henbit is a dead-nettle, a weedy flowering herb.

clue.text: Bar words ordinary folk don't understand?

definitions.text: Bar words ordinary folk don't understand?

parts.words: Bar words ordinary folk don't understand?
parts.note: the Bar is the legal profession, so its words are the jargon of lawyers that baffles laypeople

explanation.definitionFit: Lawyers' jargon is the dense technical language used in legal documents.
